title: The Fourier kernel and integrand
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring in which $p$ is invertible. Let $\pi:V\to S$ and $\pi':V'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes, put $W=V\times_S V'$, and assume $p=0$ in $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Thus $W$ is canonically an $\mathbf F_p$-scheme, including when $W$ is empty. Let $b\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ be a global function (the pairing), viewed as a morphism $b:W\to\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_p}$. Let $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\Lambda^\times$ be an additive character, meaning $\Psi(0)=1$ and $\Psi(a+a')=\Psi(a)\Psi(a')$.

Using the Artin–Schreier sheaf construction of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] with $k=\mathbf F_p$ and $q=p$, define the Fourier kernel to be the sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small étale site of $W$
$$
\mathcal K_\psi:=\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}=b^*\mathcal L_\Psi.
$$
Here $b^*$ is inverse image of étale sheaves with the same constant coefficient ring $\Lambda$; the equality is the definition of $\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}$, not an additional base-change assertion.

In the vector-bundle application, take $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ from the finite-field conventions of [def-fourier-set], with $q$ a power of $p$, let $S_0$ be a $k_0$-scheme, let $V_0\to S_0$ be a vector bundle of rank $r$, and let $V_0^\vee$ be its dual. Take $S=S_0$, $V=V_0$, $V'=V_0^\vee$, and $b(x,\xi)=\langle x,\xi\rangle$ (evaluation of a linear functional on a vector), composed with $\mathbf A^1_{S_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_p}$. On the affine line, $r=1$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and $b(x,\xi)=x\xi$, giving $\mathcal K_\psi=\mathcal L_{\Psi,x\xi}$, also denoted $\mathcal L_{\psi(x\xi)}$. In this notation $\mathcal L_{\psi(x\xi)}$ is the prime-field sheaf $\mathcal L_{\Psi,x\xi}$ just defined (Artin–Schreier construction with $k=\mathbf F_p$, pulled back along $x\xi$ composed with $\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_p}$); it is not the construction of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] with $k=k_0$ and the character $\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$, and no comparison between the two is part of this definition.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring in which $p$ is invertible, or an
admissible condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$
of [sk-def-fourier-set]. Let $\pi:V\to S$ and $\pi':V'\to S$ be morphisms of
schemes with $V\times_SV'$ of characteristic $p$, let
$b\in\Gamma(V\times_SV',\mathcal O)$ (the pairing) and let
$\Psi:\Fp\to\Lambda(*)^\times$ be an additive character. The *Fourier
kernel* is the Artin–Schreier sheaf (for $k=\Fp$) of $b$,

$$
\mathcal K_\psi:=\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}=b^*\mathcal L_\Psi ,
$$

$b$ being viewed as a morphism $V\times_SV'\to\Aone_{\Fp}$; see [sk-def-as].
For condensed $\Lambda$ it is a $\Lambda_{V\times_SV'}$-module on the
pro-étale site of $V\times_SV'$, with a finite constant local model of rank
one. For finite $\Lambda$ it may equally be read on the small étale site. In
the application $V=V_0\to S=S_0$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$,
$V'=V_0^\vee$, and $b(x,\xi)=\langle x,\xi\rangle$ is the evaluation
pairing; on $\Aone$ ($r=1$, $S_0=\Spec k_0$) this is
$\mathcal K_\psi=\mathcal L_{\psi(x\xi)}$.
